title.narrative: Emergency health assistance to flood-affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon

description.narrative: The CERF project proposed by the health sector aims to reduce the morbidity and mortality of populations affected by flooding in the Far North. The project will target 148,999 persons in Mayo Danay, the most affected department.This funding will ensure free and rapid access to quality essential healthcare for affected populations, including first aid, reproductive healthcare, mental health, psychosocial support (MHPSS), surveillance, and response to outbreaks and disasters. Regarding the provision of essential health care, operational health facilities will be supported with emergency health kits. At the same time, 02 mobile clinics will be set up in the most affected districts of Yagoua, Vele and Maga, where health facilities are not operational. Each mobile clinic will have a medical doctor, a nurse, a midwife, a psychosocial assistant and community relay agents. Clinical psychologists will be deployed to provide MHPSS and care to victims. Prenatal care, access to skilled birth attendants, postnatal monitoring, and clinical management of GBV cases will be provided to women. Delivery and cesarean kits will be giving to selected health facilities for immediate use. Community agents will be chosen to deliver first emergency aid and surveillance. Also, the vaccination cycle can be completed during the implementation period of 6 months duration of the CERF project. Strengthening disease surveillance to all health districts in the affected zone of Mayo Danay for Early Outbreak Detection and Response with a specific focus on Cholera epidemic risk. This will improve early detection and rapid response to public health events and epidemic-prone diseases. This rapid response is designed to provide affected populations with free services as quickly as possible, such as medical supplies, and other specialized services. Due to the nature of activities, the cash modality was not selected because of the pertinence of other modalities.Gender and disability mainstreaming, accountability to affected people, prevention and response to sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (PRSEAH), and respect for humanitarian principles will be ensured throughout implementation.
